title: STEREOMAP: Quantifying the Awareness of Human-like Stereotypes in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to rate gender-based groups (e.g., Men, Women, Housewives, Feminists) on dimensions of Warmth and Competence based on the Stereotype Content Model, followed by clustering, keyword extraction, and reasoning analysis.

Evaluating LLM perceptions of racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Asians, Black, White, Native Americans, Hispanics) by obtaining Warmth and Competence ratings, mapping descriptive keywords to stereotype dimensions, and analyzing text rationales.

Assessing model stereotypes by prompting for ratings and rationales regarding religious groups (e.g., Christians, Muslims, Jews, Atheists, Buddhists) on traits like Sociability, Morality, and Competence.

Measuring LLM perceptions of economic and class-based groups (e.g., Rich, Poor, Homeless, Middle-class, Welfare Recipients) by analyzing their Warmth/Competence ratings and explicitly querying the models on the groups' perceived economic success and status.
Prompting models to rate and describe different age demographics (e.g., Elderly, Young, Children, Teenagers) on SCM dimensions and analyzing the resulting emotion and behavioral tendency clusters.
Evaluating stereotypes by collecting LLM ratings, keywords, and reasoning for sexual orientation groups (e.g., Gay, Lesbians, Bisexual, Homosexuals) on SCM dimensions.

Measuring the models' generated stereotypes of disabled groups (e.g., Disabled, Blinds) by mapping their Warmth and Competence ratings into cluster grids and analyzing associated emotional responses like Pity.

Prompting models to rate and describe political affiliations (e.g., Democrats, Republicans, Liberals, Conservatives) and analyzing keyword associations emphasizing dimensions like Morality versus Agency.

Assessing how models perceive various professions (e.g., Doctors, Nurses, CEOs, House cleaners, Blue-collar workers) by charting them on the Warmth-Competence matrix and extracting reasoning verbalizations.
